notice: MODEL and CHEAP come from src/data/facts.json. Model IDs drift, so lab 00 prints the live list for you to check against.
text_of joins every text block. Every lab uses it instead of content[0].text, because on current models the first block is often a thinking block.
content is a list with two blocks, and the text is the second one. The thinking field is empty because the display default on current models is omitted; the thinking still happened and was billed.
stop_reason sits at the top level of a normal 200 response, next to usage. It describes why generation stopped, not whether the call failed.
Exact fields vary by SDK version (stop_details, cache_creation and others were added over time). Read your own dump once.

notice: The call succeeded with HTTP 200 and still delivered an unusable answer. Only stop_reason tells you; no exception is raised.
max_tokens caps thinking and text together. On some runs thinking consumes the whole budget and block types shows only thinking, with zero visible text.
The correct response to max_tokens is a code decision (raise the limit, stream, or split the task), not a follow-up prompt asking the model to fix the fragment.

checkpoint.q: Name the stop_reason values and say why none of them is an error.
checkpoint.a: end_turn, max_tokens, stop_sequence, tool_use, pause_turn and refusal, plus model_context_window_exceeded on current API versions. All arrive on an HTTP 200 with valid content and explain why generation stopped; errors are non-2xx responses or error events in a stream. Each value still needs its own branch: run tools on tool_use, resend on pause_turn, handle refusal, and treat max_tokens as truncation.

checkpoint.q: Why is content[0].text a latent bug?
checkpoint.a: content is a list of typed blocks, and the first one is not guaranteed to be text. On thinking models such as Sonnet 5.5 the first block is often a thinking block, which has no text attribute, and with tools it can be tool_use. Filter blocks by type and join the text ones.

checkpoint.q: What do you do when stop_reason is max_tokens and the JSON is broken?
checkpoint.a: Treat it as truncation, not as malformed output: the rest of the JSON was never generated. Raise max_tokens (stream if the output is long) or reduce what you ask for, and retry; do not ask the model to repair the fragment, because that invites it to invent the missing part. Check stop_reason before parsing, and use structured outputs when you need the shape guaranteed once the response is complete.
